svg.title: Blind ring: NHL '94 and NHL '95
svg.text: Through the legs: NHL '94's blind ring and NHL '95's (Genesis)
Seen from above, to scale. Each goalie faces down the page; his net is above him. Where a low puck gets no stick and no body test, it slides through him.
NHL '94: butterfly (frame 480)
the ring round the blade
NHL '95: left stick save (frame 634)
measured, one frame each spot
NHL '95: standing (ready, frame 610)
measured, one frame each spot
A round ring, 8-14 from the blade:
the blade is 9 to his side, so the ring
covers his middle: a fast low puck steps
over the sliver of body in front.
A square box (the address bug), and in
this save it sits on his middle: a channel
through him, 0-4 units from his centre.
Standing, his body is never tested (his
reach, 14, lies inside the ±14 box): only
the blade's 8 plays the puck.
NHL '94: body circle (reach 13 here; 12-15 by Agility)
NHL '94: within 8 of the blade the stick plays a low puck
NHL '94: 8-14 from the blade nothing is tested. NHL '95: untouched inside his reach (dashed)
NHL '95: the puck held or deflected there

Red: the goal line. NHL '95's maps: a slow puck (height 0) put at each spot 2 units apart, one frame played (gen95_blind_ring_check.py). In both games only a puck at height 5 or less meets the stick test.
NHL '95's stick saves, gloves and skating frames all have untouched holes inside the reach; its dive has none.
